subject: Feature portability & safe-fallback for planned tier reduction
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@healthnova.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@healthnova.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging options when stepping down from Dedicated

Hi Lauren,

We're evaluating a planned reduction from a Dedicated capacity commitment to a Hosted plan (compact/standard mix) for Q3. The execs are OK with the footprint change, but two things are blocking:

1) We currently rely on the AdvancedCache feature (keeps warm KV cache across requests) for several high-ROAS flows — can that carry over if we move to Hosted?
2) We have six months of committed credits in the current contract; will there be a fair way to translate them either into a migration credit or to preserve some burst capacity during a stepped downgrade?

I've attached a short summary of our current usage and contract ask (HealthNova_downgrade_request.pdf). Can you outline the packaging approaches and any safe-fallbacks you recommend? Ideally we need a plan that allows a rollback window in case accuracy/regression risk is higher than expected.

Thanks,
Samira
VP Growth, HealthNova

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@healthnova.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging options when stepping down from Dedicated

Hi Samira — thanks for the summary, and the PDF is helpful. TL;DR: we have a pragmatic downgrade path that preserves AdvancedCache behavior for a limited window and converts committed spend into a phased migration credit.

High-level options (quick):
- Soft downgrade (recommended pilot): Move to Compact hosted tier, enable "Feature Bridge" to retain AdvancedCache for 90 days, and allocate a temporary burst bucket for peak windows.
- Gradual roll (safe-fallback): Canary 10% of traffic on Hosted; automatic fallback to Dedicated-compatible variant if latency or generation quality drops beyond thresholds.
- Credit translation: Convert remaining committed dollars into a migration credit applied to the first 3 months on Hosting + one-time professional services (we can draft numbers).

Can I loop Karthik (runtime/ops) and Ben (pricing) to add technical and cost detail? If that looks right, propose a 30-minute sync tomorrow AM to walk the scenarios and sign off on a canary window.

Attachments: redwood_pack_matrix_v2.pdf (pack-option matrix, quick reference)

—Lauren
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@healthnova.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 14:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging options when stepping down from Dedicated

Thanks for the context — quick technical note on the options Lauren outlined so Samira has the tradeoffs documented: 

Option A — Compact hosted + Feature Bridge (90 days)
- Keeps AdvancedCache semantics by proxying cache hits through a small reserved pool. Preserves most latency characteristics for reads but adds ~5–12ms P95 overhead on writes.
- Works best if 70%+ of current active keys are hot; if your key churn is high we'll recommend a short rewarm period and prefetching.
- No model change required. Minimal QA impact.

Option B — Compact hosted + Throughput Burst add-on (no Feature Bridge)
- Lower baseline cost; relies on burst buckets (metered). Risk: cache misses may show higher latency and slight reranking regressions for tail queries.

Rollback / safe-fallback
- Canary routing (10% then 30%) with automated metrics gates (latency P95, end-to-end success, semantic-similarity regression on a small eval set). If gate fails, traffic auto-switches to Dedicated-compatible endpoint.

Implementation notes
- We can instrument a small prompt-set eval in your sandbox to measure behavioral delta during the 10% canary.
- Feature Bridge requires a short ACL add-on and a six-digit per-feature token (managed by our console).

I'll prepare a brief runbook for the canary and the feature-token lifecycle after we pick Scenario A or B.

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@healthnova.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging options when stepping down from Dedicated

Samira — a couple of concrete pricing scenarios to consider (numbers illustrative; I can produce exact figures once we have confirmed usage windows):

Scenario A (Feature Bridge + 90d) — Conservative
- Convert remaining committed dollars into: 60% migration credit applied month 1–2, 40% as professional services credit for canary/QA.
- Add-on: Feature Bridge flat fee = $12k one-time + $0.015 per 1k requests during the bridge window.
- Expected month-1 hosted spend (after credits): ~40% of prior Dedicated spend.

Scenario B (Burst + 12-month commitment) — Cost-forward
- No Feature Bridge. Provide a 10% committed-discount if HealthNova signs a 12-month hosted commitment at a blended baseline.
- We convert committed dollars into an up-front credit that covers first 4 months of hosting and a migration credit.
- Expected month-1 hosted spend (after credits): ~30–35% of prior Dedicated spend.

Other notes:
- We can carve out a 2-week rollback SLA where we guarantee access to Dedicated capacity for emergency fallbacks (operationally gated).
- I've attached pricing_scenarios_HN_v3.xlsx with worksheet tabs: "scenario_costs", "credit_conversion", "rollback_sla".

Next steps: pick A or B and confirm whether you want Feature Bridge. If you pick B and want the 10% discount, we need a headcount-style commit (baseline throughput) and a 12-month IO. Happy to jump on a 20–30 minute call to walk the workbook.

—Ben
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: pricing_scenarios_HN_v3.xlsx (pricing scenarios workbook)

From: Samira Khan <samira@healthnova.com>

Subject: Re: Packaging options when stepping down from Dedicated

Thanks everyone — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. HealthNova will proceed with Scenario B (Burst + 12-month commitment) and take the 10% committed-discount; we want the migration credit applied as you outlined. Procurement will follow up with an IO/term sheet next week.

Please go ahead and schedule the technical kickoff (canary plan) for Monday morning — cc'ing our procurement lead.

Best,
Samira
VP Growth, HealthNova
